draft.title: Shapes and objects
card: Shapes
A 2D shape is flat. It is described by its sides and angles. A triangle has 3 sides and 3 angles. A rectangle has 4 sides and 4 right angles (90°).
Objects
A 3D object takes up space. It is described by its faces (flat surfaces), edges (where two faces meet) and vertices (corners). A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices.
Composite
A composite shape or object is made by joining simpler ones. An L-shape is two rectangles joined. A house can be a rectangular prism with a triangular prism as its roof.
To describe a composite, split it into simple parts and name each part. For example, a tent shape with a rectangle below a triangle is a pentagon with 5 sides.
draft.remember: Shapes have sides and angles. Objects have faces, edges and vertices. Composites are built from simple parts.

a.q: How many faces does a rectangular prism (a box shape) have?
a.why: A box has a top, a bottom and four sides, so 6 faces. 12 is the number of edges and 8 is the number of vertices, which are different parts of the object.
a.clue: Faces are the flat surfaces. Count top, bottom and sides.

b.q: Jo draws a flat shape made of a square with an equilateral triangle joined along one of its sides, with no gap. How many sides does the new outline have?
b.why: The square has 4 sides and the triangle has 3, which makes 7. The shared side is inside the shape, so it is not on the outline. Both shapes lose it, so 7 − 2 = 5 sides. 7 is tempting because it counts the shared side twice.
b.clue: The joined side is no longer on the outside.

problems.detail: The last bullet says to split a composite into simple parts and name each part, but its example names the whole outline as a pentagon instead of naming the parts. The example is also only a pentagon if the triangle's base matches the rectangle's width, which the card does not say.

check.summary: Both questions are correct: a box has 6 faces, and a square with a triangle joined along one side has a 5-sided outline. One minor card issue: the composite example names the whole outline instead of its parts, and does not say the triangle's base must match the rectangle's width.
